questions.q: What mechanism keeps a physical standby database current with the primary?
options: Redo Apply — continuous media recovery applying shipped redo directly to the standby's data files
SQL Apply — redo mined into SQL statements and re-executed
A nightly full backup restore from the primary
Manual re-creation of the standby every time the primary changes
questions.explain: A physical standby is block-for-block identical and stays current via Redo Apply, essentially perpetual media recovery.

questions.q: What mechanism keeps a logical standby current, and what does it produce?
options: SQL Apply, which mines redo via LogMiner and re-executes it as SQL, producing a database that is logically but not physically identical to the primary
Redo Apply, producing a block-for-block identical copy
A manual daily export/import job
It doesn't stay current automatically at all
questions.explain: SQL Apply reconstructs and replays SQL statements from mined redo, so the data matches logically while the physical structure can differ.

questions.q: What capability does a logical standby have that a physical standby (without Active Data Guard) does not?
options: It's continuously open read-write for its own extra objects, such as additional indexes or tables not on the primary, without needing a separate license
It applies redo faster than a physical standby in every case
It requires no license of any kind, while a physical standby always requires Active Data Guard
It can never be used for disaster recovery
questions.explain: A logical standby stays open read-write for supplementary objects at all times; a plain physical standby needs the licensed Active Data Guard option just for read-only queries during apply.

questions.q: What is a real limitation of a logical standby compared to a physical standby?
options: SQL Apply doesn't support every data type and every DDL operation, so it isn't a guaranteed drop-in replacement
A logical standby cannot ever be queried
A logical standby cannot exist on a different server than the primary
A logical standby always has less storage capacity than the primary
questions.explain: SQL Apply has documented data type and DDL support gaps, which physical standbys, being exact copies, don't have.

questions.q: Which command starts a physical standby applying shipped redo?
options: ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE USING CURRENT LOGFILE DISCONNECT FROM SESSION
ALTER DATABASE START LOGICAL STANDBY APPLY
EXEC DBMS_STATS.GATHER_TABLE_STATS
EXPLAIN PLAN FOR SELECT * FROM standby_status
questions.explain: RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE begins Redo Apply (continuous media recovery) for a physical standby; START LOGICAL STANDBY APPLY is the logical-standby equivalent using SQL Apply.
